hints: She wrote it after many years of living with the gorillas.
It came out after she had studied gorillas in Rwanda for well over a decade.
The film with Sigourney Weaver came out five years after the book.
questions.fun_fact: Fossey first went to Rwanda in 1967 and set up her research camp high between two volcanoes.

questions.question: In 1916, Jeannette Rankin became the first woman elected to the US Congress, four years before the 19th Amendment. Which state elected her?
hints: It is a big Western state.
Its nickname is “Big Sky Country.”
Its capital is Helena.
questions.fun_fact: Rankin was the only member of Congress to vote against US entry into both World War I and World War II.

hints: The poet was Amanda Gorman.
Presidents take the oath of office here.
Congress meets inside me.
questions.fun_fact: Amanda Gorman was the youngest poet ever to read at a US presidential inauguration.

hints: It sits on the Mississippi River.
It is in Missouri.
It is famous for its huge Gateway Arch.
questions.fun_fact: Josephine Baker adopted 12 children from around the world and called them her “Rainbow Tribe.”

It was just a few years after the Civil War.
It came half a century before the 19th Amendment.

hints: My invention is called the Laserphaco Probe.
I also helped start the field of community eye care.
My first name is Patricia.
questions.fun_fact: Patricia Bath's laser tool has helped bring sight back to people who had been blind for decades.

questions.description: A launch so late at night it needed its own nightlight.

Sally Ride flew on the same shuttle earlier that year.
This shuttle was lost in 1986.
questions.fun_fact: Bluford's mission, STS-8, also made the shuttle's first night landing.

questions.description: His cats had more toes than usual, and his life had more adventures than most.
questions.question: “I drove an ambulance in World War I, loved boxing and deep-sea fishing, and kept six-toed cats in Key West. Who am I?”
hints: I won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1954.
I lived for years in Cuba.
I wrote “The Old Man and the Sea.”
questions.fun_fact: About 60 cats live at Hemingway's old home in Key West, and many still have six toes.

Inside it, the wind can suddenly go almost still.
You see the world with two of these.
questions.fun_fact: The eye of a hurricane can be calm and sunny, but the strongest winds of the whole storm spin in the wall of clouds right around it.

hints: There are five of them.
One of them is called Lake Superior.
Their name says they're really big.

It can come from the sea.
